newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares end 2.16 percent higher.
newsitem.headline: French shares end 2.16 percent higher.

text.p: French shares closed sharply higher on Monday as sentiment changed as dramatically as the weather and Wall Street and the dollar surged ahead after last week's falls.
The CAC-40 blue-chip index closed 2.16 percent higher at 2,572.31, below the day's high of 2,589.11.
April futures were 67 points up at 2,583. Volume was 5.1 billion francs.
Dealers said the U.S. markets were boosted by the prospect of further interest rate rises. European bond markets were also firm.
Synthelabo was the biggest riser, up 6.42 percent at 597 francs, ahead of an analysts' meeting on Tuesday and resurging merger rumours.
Galeries Lafayette added 5.98 percent to 2,305 francs after the retailer reported on Friday evening that it returned to profit in 1996 with net earnings of 550 million francs.
Dassault Systemes gained 5.89 percent to 355.80. It and SGS-Thomson, both also listed in New York, were pulled higher by Wall Street's technology stocks run.

Renault also rose more than five percent, adding 5.46 percent to 139 francs, boosted by a Spanish car buy incentive. Spain is its second-largest export market. Dealers also cited relief that while two recent judgments rapped Renault for failing to consult with worker representatives before announcing the Vilvoorde plant closure, the rulings have no bearing on the decision itself and are not expected to delay it.
Eridania-Beghin Say SA dropped 4.29 percent to 871 francs as the market responded negatively to the agro-food company's cautious outlook on its 1997 results, dealers said.
